subject: Data handling: residency/retention and redaction options for MedSys integration
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@medsyshealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: MedSys Compliance <compliance@medsyshealth.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on retention windows + redaction for PHI/PII intake

Hi Soojin,

Quick intro: I'm Julia on the MedSys integrations team. We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will route clinical intake forms and care-coordination chat logs through your hosted API. Before we proceed I need clarity on a couple of compliance items so we can sign off internally:

- Recommended retention limits for different classes (identifiers vs clinical text) for US-regulated PHI workloads. We are considering a 12-month default but want to understand tradeoffs.
- Redaction vs pseudonymization: typical approaches you support, how reversible pseudonymization is handled, and what you can guarantee about irreversible redaction.
- How does Redwood handle temporary artifacts like KV cache or streaming buffers — are those ever persisted beyond the request?
- Evidence of deletion: can you provide verifiable logs/audit entries suitable for our legal team if we request a deletion for a tenant?

I've attached a short SOW and a scope doc for the pilot. Can we get a short options summary we can present to our security and legal teams by end of week?

Thanks,
Julia Park
MedSys Health — Integrations
julia.park@medsyshealth.com
Attachment: SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 145KB)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@medsyshealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Aug 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on retention windows + redaction for PHI/PII intake

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I'll loop in Marissa and Karthik for operational and legal details. We can follow up with a 30-min compliance deep-dive and a short mutual action plan.

1) Retention guidance (recommended starting defaults):
   - Direct identifiers (name, SSN, DOB, MRN): 30 days to 90 days by default; 12 months only with explicit business justification and contract language.
   - Sensitive structured PHI elements (diagnoses, meds tied to an ID): 90 days to 1 year depending on downstream use.
   - Unstructured clinical text (notes, chat transcripts): 180 days to 1 year; consider sampling or selective retention for model fine-tuning.
   - Embeddings/derived vectors: treat as sensitive if reversible or linkable; recommend 90 days unless encrypted and access-controlled.

2) Redaction vs pseudonymization:
   - Irreversible redaction: we can support field-level replace-with-token (e.g., [REDACTED_PATIENT_NAME]) implemented in our ingestion pipeline. Once redacted data is overwritten and deleted from transient stores and archives, reversal is not possible.
   - Reversible pseudonymization: we offer tokenization with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) so identifiers can be re-linked if keys exist. This is reversible only while keys are retained. We recommend customer KMS for legal/escrow controls.

3) Temporary artifacts (KV cache, streaming buffers):
   - KV cache is in-memory per-server with TTLs. By default we do not persist request bodies to disk. Caches used for long-running chat sessions have configurable TTLs (default 1 hour) and are not backed up to long-term storage.

4) Evidence and audit:
   - Deletion requests generate audit logs with timestamps, actor IDs, and affected object IDs. For Dedicated/Private customers we can provide stronger deletion proofs (signed deletion receipts) and longer audit retention per contract.

Next steps: Marissa can attach our redaction playbook summary and examples of delete receipts. If MedSys wants a 12-month policy we'll need to escalate to Pricing + Legal (contract amendment).

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Trust & Compliance — Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@medsyshealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Aug 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on retention windows + redaction for PHI/PII intake

Julia — adding a few operational details so your security team has concrete controls to evaluate:

- Ingestion pipeline: we run a classification + extraction step on ingest. Identifiers can be routed to a pseudonymization path or redaction transform before any downstream processing. Customers can opt to have originals written to an encrypted archive with a configurable retention window (30/60/90 days) for debugging.

- Archive & keys: archives are AES-256 encrypted; KMS keys are customer-managed for Private deployments or Redwood-managed with strict access controls for Hosted. For reversible pseudonymization, we recommend customer KMS with a key rotation policy and optional escrow under an executed agreement.

- Deletion proof: on deletion we can provide an audit bundle containing: deletion request meta, object IDs, storage manifests showing truncation, and signed hash of deletion event. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your SIEM; for hosted we'll provide downloadable receipts.

- Legal hold / emergency access: we support hold flags which suspend automated destruction and produce a bindable audit record. Reversal of pseudonyms during a hold requires key access or legal process depending on who controls the keys.

Attached is a 2-page redaction-playbook summary to give example flows. Happy to walk through it.

—Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, Customer Security
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachment: redaction-playbook-summary.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 78KB)
From: Julia Park <julia.park@medsyshealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, MedSys Compliance <compliance@medsyshealth.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Aug 2028 08:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on retention windows + redaction for PHI/PII intake

Thanks — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from Legal/Compliance after a quick read: 

- MedSys would prefer a 12-month default for unstructured clinical text and derived embeddings for pilot continuity; is there a material cost delta or operational risk we should call out?
- For reversible pseudonymization, assume MedSys will insist on customer KMS with key escrow only under court process. Can Redwood support HSM-backed key management and an escrow workflow?
- Can you outline the shortest possible end-to-end deletion SLA (from request to evidence delivered) for hosted vs dedicated customers?

If we can get those three quick answers today we can move to an MSA amendment draft.

—Julia
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@medsyshealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Aug 2028 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on retention windows + redaction for PHI/PII intake

Julia — answers inline and a recommended path forward.

- 12-month retention cost/risk:
  * Hosted: 12 months increases storage and audit retention costs; approximate run-rate increase for embedding/notes-heavy workloads is ~12–18% on monthly bill, plus longer audit retention fees. Operational risk: longer windows increase exposure surface for potential misuse and increase complexity of deletions.
  * Dedicated/Private: cost is primarily infra/ops; we can provide fixed pricing for a 12-month commit. If MedSys needs contractual guarantees on retention windows we advise Dedicated or Private.

- HSM-backed KMS & escrow:
  * Yes — Redwood supports customer-managed KMS that integrates with HSM-backed providers (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM, others). Escrow workflows are supported for Private deployments and available as an add-on for Dedicated with legal terms. Hosted customers can supply external keys for tokenization but escrow still requires contract terms.

- Deletion SLA (shortest practical):
  * Hosted: 48–72 hours to execute deletion and provide audit bundle for tenant-scoped object deletes (subject to verification and queueing).
  * Dedicated/Private: 24–48 hours with signed deletion receipt and SIEM integration where applicable.

Recommended path:
 1) For the pilot, we can enable reversible pseudonymization with customer-managed KMS (HSM) and a 12-month retention for unstructured text only; identifiers will be redacted after 90 days unless you explicitly request re-linking.
 2) Create a short MSA amendment that covers key custody, escrow conditions, deletion SLAs, and pricing for extended retention. We can draft this and include the redaction-playbook excerpt.
 3) Schedule a 45-minute compliance workshop next week (Soojin + Marissa + Karthik + MedSys security/legal).

If you confirm pilot choices I will ask Sales to prepare the MSA amendment and Pricing to estimate the delta.

Thanks — feel free to drop times for the workshop and we'll lock it.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Director, Trust & Compliance — Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
